sample_data.method: bundled in source (imported directly from P06_client_digest_public.json at build time, no upload needed)
sample_data.reset_instructions: Refresh the page to reload the original fixture data. The alert control resets to the default alert from the JSON on refresh; no manual reset action is required since no data is mutated or persisted.

problem_solving_method: Parsed the provided monthly client metrics fixture and built a small set of pure functions to compute month-over-month change, percent change, and direction per measure. Top movers are ranked by absolute percent change (not raw difference) so measures on different scales can be fairly compared. A summary sentence is generated per client directly from the computed top movers. All client reports render together as a batch view, with a live alert control (measure, direction, level) that recalculates which clients cross the threshold on demand.

R1.evidence: src/lib/data.js loads the fixture; 10 clients with 7 measures each and two months of history (last/current) are present, exceeding the minimum of 6 clients and 5 measures

R2.evidence: src/lib/metrics.js (calculateChange, processClient) computes current value, change with direction, and top 2 movers per client; rendered per-client in src/lib/render.js (renderClientCard)

R3.evidence: src/lib/metrics.js (generateSummary) builds a summary sentence from each client's actual computed top movers; displayed on every client card, e.g. 'Khulna Motors saw Sessions dropped by 57.4%, while Conversion Rate improved by 51.7%.'

R4.evidence: src/main.js and src/lib/render.js (renderAlertControl, processBatch) render all client reports at once and let the user set measure/direction/level; clients crossing the threshold show an alert badge live on 'Apply Alert'

team_members.major_contribution: Built the full solution independently: data loading, core calculation logic (change/percent/direction), top-mover ranking, summary generation, alert system, Tailwind UI, unit tests, and deployment

major_design_decisions: Ranked top movers by absolute percent change rather than raw numeric difference, so measures on very different scales (e.g. Spend vs. CTR) can be fairly compared
Handled zero-value edge cases explicitly (previous value of 0) by returning a null percent change instead of dividing by zero or showing Infinity
Used no backend or database, since the data is a static test fixture and client-side processing was sufficient within the time limit
Kept alert configuration in in-memory JS state rather than persisting it, since persistence was not required by the problem statement
known_limitations: Only the PUB-01 test case from the provided JSON is used; the app does not support switching between multiple cases if the file contains more than one
Alert configuration resets on page refresh and is not saved between sessions
Unit tests cover the core calculation logic but not the UI rendering layer directly

ai_tools_used.used_for: Explaining the problem statement, designing the calculation and alert logic, debugging setup issues, structuring the Tailwind UI, writing unit tests, and drafting documentation (README.md, this manifest)
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: All generated code was run locally, manually tested in-browser against the provided sample data, and checked against automated Vitest unit tests before being committed and deployed
